If I may rephrase your question slightly, to 'Should the minimum wage be set to a level that allows people to live comfortably while earning it?' I would say no.

Ultimately, we (society) want to reduce poverty. We want people, at the very minimum, to be able to afford the basic necessities of life, and if possible thrive and live comfortably. Minimum wage laws (in my opinion) seek to accomplish this in the short term by imposing arbitrary rules, but actually have the opposite effect in the long term.

Some points I'll make, I'd be happy to discuss any at length:

  • Setting a minimum wage only makes lower-paying jobs illegal. Having fewer jobs in the economy isn't a good thing. Someone making less than minimum wage is still better off than someone making nothing.
  • Setting a minimum wage forces employers to raise the cost of their goods/services, which forces customers to raise their costs to match, this all leads to a spiral of inflation and those who were making minimum wage have just as much (or little) buying power as before.
  • Raising minimum wage forces employers to lay off staff in the short term.
  • A wage is a contract agreed upon by two willing, free, informed parties, the employer and the employee, and neither would agree to it if it didn't benefit them both. There's no need for government to interfere in this transaction.
